question: Examine whether the vectors $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=4\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ are equal. Also determine their directional relationship and justify your answer.
explanation:
Step 1: Comparison of corresponding components
The corresponding components of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are not equal. Therefore, the vectors cannot be equal.
Step 2: Proportionality test
Observe that
\(\vec{b}=2(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k})=2\vec{a}\)
Step 3: Directional interpretation
One non-zero vector is a positive scalar multiple of the other. Hence, the vectors are parallel and point in the same direction.
Step 4: Equality condition
Equal vectors must have both the same magnitude and the same direction. Here, $|\vec{b}|=2|\vec{a}|$, so their magnitudes differ.
Final Answer
The vectors are not equal. They are parallel and have the same direction.

options.A: The vectors are equal because their corresponding components are proportional.
options.B: The vectors are not equal; $\vec{b}=2\vec{a}$, so they are parallel, have the same direction, and $|\vec{b}|=2|\vec{a}|$.
options.C: The vectors are not equal and are parallel in opposite directions because $\vec{b}=-2\vec{a}$.
options.D: The vectors are perpendicular because their magnitudes differ.
